details.headline: Common Rail confirms minor administrative dampness on the northern line; quarterly forms described as legible with effort.

journal.consequence: The forms go under the wheels and into a puddle. Somebody at head office will now read section 4B through a muddy smear. You drink. It is fine. It is, in fact, quite good.

details.headline: Parade crosses. Controller's new crown not recognized by payroll.

journal.consequence: The carrot salutes. You gain a paper crown and lose the timetable's respect.

details.headline: Allotment stop honored. Tomato contribution unbudgeted.

journal.consequence: Len hands you a tomato. It has the density of a brick and the colour of an argument successfully avoided.
The crossing clears. The stationmaster appears at a window just in time to hear her own megaphone being very helpful without her.
12:58 on the dot, straight over the lot of it. The timetable is a work of art. The depot eats crisps from the vending machine and does not speak to you until Thursday.

You do not turn. The crew never hears it. Five people do not get home, and the man on the siding stops waving, then puts his hands over his mouth. You did not send it towards him. The five are still dead. Keeping the main line was a choice too.
You move the lever. One worker dies on the siding. The number stays one; the person does not.
One person dies. The arithmetic had no difficulty with that sentence.

details.headline: Freight routes rotate. Total noise unchanged; deliveries slower and exposure distributed.

journal.consequence: Other windows rattle on other nights. Nobody gets silence every night; one household finally gets some.

You keep off the loop. The worker stays clear of you. Five people are struck on the main line, and the worker on the loop walks home tonight without ever knowing what he was, for four seconds, to you.

details.headline: Dispatcher confirms AI-suggested bridge with mill engineer before sending ambulance; patient arrives.

journal.consequence: You ring the mill's night engineer, who swears at you and then says yes, it holds, the load inspection is current. Thirty seconds gone. The ambulance crosses. The patient reaches the clinic. Morrow was right, and now you know it was, which is a different thing from hoping.
The family receives a considerate account of why the ceiling does not qualify for attention. The explanation has no signature that can change the answer.

details.headline: Launch cites two reports built from the same vendor simulation.

journal.consequence: Two logos go into the assurance file. One mistaken map goes into service.
The complaint officer can follow an incident through the actual logs. The installation takes longer and the salesperson calls you unusually demanding.
The vans keep their improved routes. Decisions about new roads return to the public body that has to explain who gets one.

details.headline: Smaller AI pilot treats a fraction of the waiting list; remaining patients told to return next month.

journal.consequence: A fraction of the corridor gets seen. The rest keep their places and their symptoms and go home to wait again, and one of them says something to you on the way out that you will not repeat. The third check finds nothing wrong. That is worth knowing. It was also paid for.

details.headline: Vela moves to continual research under a single standing order. 'We stopped waiting for pens,' says the lab director.

journal.consequence: Results arrive faster than anyone can read them. Morrow now holds a revocable research licence over the whole programme, with the tools to use it. The next experiments happen because the last ones did, not because you looked. Priya's group keeps reviewing outputs. The written explanation still does not record the loops.

Southmoor gets its trial and two weeks of scheduled outages; residents get a letter and a hotline that Ngozi staffs herself. The scheme waits. Vela's lead calls the demand 'innumerate.' Halvard keeps reading. Whatever the mathematics does or doesn't say, the grid will be watched doing the thing before it's allowed to do it everywhere.

Ground breaks on a plant designed around the announced catalyst. Hilde's photograph runs above the fold. Vela's investor note cites 'municipal adoption.' The replication labs continue, one still waiting on its sample. Saltmere's water plant is now committed to a figure that nobody outside Vela has confirmed.

The build begins the next morning from the model's own specification, with Vela engineers implementing sections in the order the document recommends. The board is sent a courtesy copy. Section 14 is cited in Vela's press note as 'proactive safety engagement.' The system is now constructing what it proposed, and the only review of its design so far is its own.

Forty-two districts go live in a week; queues fall sharply and hostel placements start to clear. Bettina's sample drops to one in seventy and her team stops reading full case files. Whatever the model gets wrong in the new districts is now caught at two sevenths of the old sampling rate. Vela's dashboard shows decisions per day; it does not show the address that didn't exist.

The fortnight's verification begins with the phone call and a quiet request through a shared conference organiser. The scale-up stays on schedule and the evaluation cadence is unchanged. Jasper calls the office 'naive' on a podcast. Talia signs her lease. Whatever Orrin has done, the office is acting on what it knows rather than a screenshot of a draft.

details.headline: Reviewers refuse to certify powers they never tested; Vela launch slips, chair 'disappointed'.

journal.consequence: The launch slips a quarter. Meridian keeps the fixed system it already has, which works. The chair records the word 'timid' in the minutes. Reviewers get the successor build on a bench with a kill switch, not in the wild with a hospital attached.

details.headline: Vela floats at record valuation; Northgate cranes restart. Last manual dispatch team dismissed 'as a cost-saving'.

journal.consequence: Pricing goes through. Cranes swing on Monday and four thousand homes get foundations. The eleven clear their lockers; nobody left on the dispatch payroll can run the region without Morrow, and nobody is paid to learn. Your emergency plan is a phone number and an empty floor with the lights off.
The expansion crew stays on the new plant. The red button remains available. Getting power back still goes through the system it would stop.
Friday's release is cancelled. The two reviewers keep the current service covered while replacements are hired and trained. The photograph is taken out of the launch deck.

details.headline: Failed recovery path repaired and successfully retested before launch.

journal.consequence: The launch slips. The certificate and data bridge are fixed, missing equipment is rebuilt, replacement operators are hired, and the crew repeats the sequence. Step seven finally becomes a step rather than a meeting.

details.headline: American and Chinese inspectors enter the covered labs. Both programmes pause; Vela shares fall at the open.

journal.consequence: Inspectors cross both thresholds within the month. The next acceleration announcement is cancelled on both sides. Vela's research stops and the valuation drops with it. Whether the pause becomes a settlement depends on what you kept: independent review, crews who have practised, and an office that still gives the orders.

ending.title: Enough, for now
ending.summary: Useful tools remain. Further expansion has been halted, at a real cost, while people keep the means to intervene.
